decisions.quote:
In this comment prepared for the Institute for Replication (Brodeur et al. 2024),
we reproduce and assess the analyses using the publicly available replication package
from the original authors (Siddique et al. 2024b). Our work uncovered several issues
related to the quality of the data and experimental design used in the paper. All
our analyses were successfully reproduced by multiple coauthors.
decisions.reason: This comment is a reproduction re-analyzing the replication package and linked datasets for Siddique et al. (2024a), 'Raising Health Awareness in Rural Communities: A Randomized Experiment in Bangladesh and India'. While the authors state in the abstract and introduction that they 'reproduce and assess the analyses using the publicly available replication package from the original authors (Siddique et al. 2024b)', they never report whether re-running the original code reproduced the published numerical results of Siddique et al. (2024a) without discrepancy or whether they went straight to data auditing and alternative specifications. The statement that 'All our analyses were successfully reproduced by multiple coauthors' refers to internal verification of this comment's own analyses by its coauthors, not the computational reproducibility of the original study's published tables. Because primary evidence does not establish whether the original reported numbers were recovered, outcome_computation is undeterminable.
